text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- All ministers have been given special tasks to boost the country's economic situation this year, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.
-- The Cabinet has directed Kuala Lumpur City Hall to introduce special lanes for buses in the city, Entrepreneur Development Minister Mustapa Mohamed said.

-- The International Natural Rubber Organisation is expected to adopt a "different approach" in its management and price intervention policies when a Malaysian assumes the top post of the organisation.
-- There is no longer any necessity for Malaysia to borrow from abroad as there is sufficient amount of money that can be tapped to meet financing needs, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.

-- The ringgit surged to an eight-month high yesterday, strengthening by 100 basis points against the U.S. dollar. Dealers were crediting offshore buyers, from London to Tokyo, for the sharp rebound of the Malaysian currency.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad urged youths to uphold sel-dicipline and reject punk culture and other negative Western trends.
